easy.def: Very angry.
examples: The irate man shouted.
She was irate.
An irate customer.

more.def: Extremely angry.
examples: The irate customer demanded a refund.
She was irate when she saw the muddy floor.
An irate goose chased us.

easy.def: Shining with changing colors.
examples: The bubble was iridescent.
Iridescent wings.
An iridescent shell.

more.def: Showing shining colors that seem to change as you move.
examples: The soap bubble was iridescent.
The dragonfly had iridescent wings.
The shell shone with iridescent colors.

easy.def: A tall flower with big, bright colors.
examples: An iris grew in the garden.
The iris is purple.
I picked an iris.

more.def: A tall garden flower with long, thin leaves and large, colorful blooms.
examples: Purple irises grew along the edge of the pond.
The iris bloomed in late spring.
Grandma planted rows of yellow irises by the fence.

easy.def: The colored part of your eye.
examples: The iris of her eye is brown.
My iris is blue.
The colored ring is the iris.

more.def: The round, colored part of the eye that surrounds the black center.
examples: The iris of her eye was a deep green.
The iris opens and closes to let in more or less light.
A cat's iris can be yellow or green.

easy.def: A hard, strong metal.
examples: The gate is made of iron.
Iron is a metal.
The bridge is iron.

more.def: A hard, strong metal that is used to make tools, nails and many other things.
examples: The fence is made of iron.
Iron rusts when it gets wet.
A magnet sticks to iron.

easy.def: A tool that you heat to make clothes smooth.
examples: Dad used an iron on the shirt.
The iron is hot.
Be careful with the iron.

more.def: A flat, heated tool used to press wrinkles out of clothes.
examples: Dad used an iron to smooth the wrinkles in his shirt.
The iron is very hot, so do not touch it.
Mom ironed the shirt with a steam iron.

easy.def: The opposite of what you would expect.
examples: It was ironic.
An ironic joke.
The ironic ending.

more.def: Happening in a way that is the opposite of what you would expect.
examples: It was ironic that the fire station caught fire.
The ironic twist made everyone laugh.
It was ironic that the weather forecaster forgot his umbrella.

easy.def: Things made of metal.
examples: The gate has ironwork.
The ironwork is black.
The ironwork is old.

more.def: Things made of iron, such as gates, railings and decorations.
examples: The old gate had fancy ironwork.
The balcony had curly ironwork.
The ironwork was black and strong.

easy.def: When things turn out the opposite of what you expect.
examples: There was irony in the story.
The irony made us laugh.
That is irony.

more.def: A funny or strange situation where what happens is the opposite of what you would expect.
examples: The irony was that the baker could not bake.
It was an irony that the fire station burned down.
There was a touch of irony in his voice.

easy.def: Not making sense.
examples: An irrational fear.
It was irrational.
The irrational idea.

more.def: Not based on clear thinking; not sensible.
examples: He had an irrational fear of the dark.
It was irrational to be afraid of a kitten.
The irrational plan made no sense.

easy.def: Not even or not in a regular way.
examples: The path is irregular.
The shape was irregular.
She had irregular sleep.

more.def: Not smooth, even or regular in shape or pattern, or not following the usual rule.
examples: The coastline has an irregular shape with many bays and points.
The word "went" is an irregular verb because it does not end in -ed.
The old clock ticked at irregular times.

easy.def: Having nothing to do with the matter.
examples: That is irrelevant.
An irrelevant fact.
The irrelevant question.

more.def: Not connected to what is being talked about.
examples: His comment about pizza was irrelevant to the lesson.
The teacher ignored the irrelevant question.
That detail is irrelevant to the story.

easy.def: So special it cannot be replaced.
examples: The old toy is irreplaceable.
An irreplaceable photo.
My dog is irreplaceable.

more.def: So special or rare that nothing else can take its place.
examples: The old family photo is irreplaceable.
A good friend is irreplaceable.
The antique vase was irreplaceable.

easy.def: So good that you cannot say no.
examples: The warm cookies were irresistible.
That puppy is irresistible.
The pool looked irresistible.

more.def: So tempting or so charming that you cannot stop yourself from wanting it.
examples: The smell of fresh pancakes was irresistible, so we all got out of bed.
The baby's giggle was irresistible and made everyone laugh too.
On such a hot day, the cool lake looked irresistible.

easy.def: In a way you cannot say no to.
examples: The cake was irresistibly sweet.
The kitten was irresistibly cute.
She was irresistibly drawn.

more.def: In a way that is so attractive or strong that you cannot say no.
examples: The puppy was irresistibly cute.
The smell of cookies drew us irresistibly to the kitchen.
The river flowed irresistibly toward the sea.

easy.def: Not careful about what you should do.
examples: It is irresponsible to leave the gate open.
He was irresponsible with his toys.
That was an irresponsible thing to do.

more.def: Not acting in a careful or sensible way, so that you let others down.
examples: It was irresponsible of him to leave the stove on.
Leaving a campfire burning is irresponsible and could hurt the forest.
The irresponsible driver forgot to check his mirrors before turning.

easy.def: To bring water to dry land for plants.
examples: Farmers irrigate the fields.
The farm irrigates its crops.
They irrigated the land.

more.def: To supply dry land with water by using pipes or ditches.
examples: Farmers irrigate their fields in summer.
The ditch irrigated the dry farm.
They irrigated the desert so crops could grow.

easy.def: Bringing water to dry land for plants.
examples: The farm needs irrigation.
Irrigation waters the crops.
The irrigation ditch is full.

more.def: The act of bringing water to dry land through pipes or ditches so crops can grow.
examples: The farm uses irrigation to water the crops.
Irrigation ditches carry water to the fields.
Without irrigation, the desert fields would be dry.

easy.def: Cranky and easy to make angry.
examples: He is irritable when he is tired.
The baby was irritable.
Mom was irritable this morning.

more.def: Easily annoyed or in a bad mood, especially when tired or hungry.
examples: My little brother gets irritable when he misses his nap.
The long, hot ride made everyone irritable.
She felt irritable because of the loud noise outside.

easy.def: In a cross way.
examples: He answered irritably.
She spoke irritably.
The tired baby cried irritably.

more.def: In a cross or impatient way, because you are annoyed.
examples: He answered irritably because he was tired and hungry.
"Not now!" she said irritably.
The cat flicked its tail irritably.

easy.def: Something that bothers you.
examples: Dust is an irritant.
The irritant made me sneeze.
The irritant stung.

more.def: Something that annoys you or causes discomfort, such as dust in the eyes.
examples: Dust is an irritant to my eyes.
The noise was a constant irritant.
Pollen is an irritant for many people.

easy.def: To bother someone or make something sore.
examples: The noise irritates me.
The wool irritates my skin.
Smoke irritates my eyes.

more.def: To make someone annoyed, or to make part of the body red, itchy or sore.
examples: The loud tapping began to irritate everyone in the quiet room.
Wool can irritate sensitive skin and make it itchy.
The cold wind irritated her eyes.

easy.def: Annoying.
examples: The noise is irritating.
An irritating buzz.
It is irritating.

more.def: Annoying, so that it makes you feel bothered or upset.
examples: The irritating buzz of the fly kept me awake.
It was irritating to wait so long.
The tag on my shirt was irritating.

easy.def: Feeling annoyed, or a sore spot.
examples: He felt irritation.
A skin irritation.
The noise caused irritation.

more.def: A feeling of being annoyed, or a sore place on the skin.
examples: He felt irritation at the loud noise.
The soap caused a skin irritation.
Her irritation grew as she waited.
